doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Views on jazz, race and Europe
title: Why Latin and hyphenated jazz is not jazz to him
summary: Heath disagrees with Dizzy that all world music will merge, insisting that jazz must keep its own rhythm.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And the Latin thing too, right? From Cuba?

Well, you see, the Latin thing, they had their own thing as far as I’m concerned. The rhythm was there, but to me, contrary to what Dizzy said, he said all the music of the world is going to be the same. I disagree with that, ‘cause jazz will always be jazz as far as I’m concerned. If you put Latino rhythms or whatever, it’s hyphenated. Free jazz, funk jazz, if you gotta hyphenate it, it’s sort of diluted, for me, ‘cause I believe that [sings jazz drum beat], that rhythm must always be a part of jazz, to me, not that Latin thing, which is great to dance by. It’s great. And African music itself, it’s not jazz either. But that’s my own narrow-minded concept of what the music should be.
We’ll say that in quotation marks.
